etymologies.etymologyHTML: Attested since the 15th century C.E.; from Middle English supervisor, supervisour, supervysor, supervysour, from Latin supervīsor, from supervideō, in turn from super + videō. By surface analysis, supervise +‎ -or.

definitions.definition: (management) A person with the official task of overseeing the work of a person or group, or of other operations and activities.

quote.text: Thus, today, even if the objective does seem "goalish," the supervisor assumes the problem inherent in trying to "accomplish" that goal will become clear to the librarian as the action plan evolves  […]

quote.citation: 2001, Wendy Dobson, Gary Hufbauer, World Capital Markets‎[1], →ISBN, page 103:
quote.text: The 1999 merger between Citibank (banking) and Travelers (insurance) created the model for megafinance and confirmed new challenges for supervisors.

quote.citation: 2012, Kathryn M. Johnson, The Insider's Guide to Supervising Government Employees‎[2]:
quote.text: I had learned a lot about supervising by observing other supervisors—the good things and the not-so-good things they did.

definitions.definition: A person who monitors someone to make sure they comply with rules or other requirements set for them.

quote.citation: 2013, Thomas Pynchon, Bleeding Edge, Vintage, published 2014, page 24:
quote.text: Kashruth fraud in Brooklyn. Seems a goon squad of fake mashgichim or kosher supervisors have been making their way around the neighborhoods pulling surprise ‘inspections’ on different shops and restaurants, selling them fancy-looking certificates to put in the window  […]

definitions.definition: (US) In certain states, an elected member of the governing body for a county which is called the board of supervisors.
(computing) A process responsible for managing other processes.

quote.citation: 1965, P. A. Crisman, The compatible time-sharing system: a programmer's guide, page 14:
quote.text: The clock burst which enables the supervisor to housekeep the console input and output and to change program status is currently set to 200 ms.
